summary: This House resolution expresses the sense that Congress and the Department of Transportation should work together to reach zero roadway deaths by 2050 by advancing safety policies, improving crash data, implementing proven countermeasures, and adopting a safe-systems approach.

scores.thoughts: The resolution expresses a sense of the House regarding traffic safety goals and calls on the Department of Transportation to implement countermeasures, but contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any government expenditures or budgets. It is a non-binding expression of intent with no fiscal implications.
The bill text makes no reference to taxes, tax policy, revenue measures, or any changes to the tax code.
While the preamble notes traffic fatalities and injuries, the resolution itself does not address healthcare systems, coverage, delivery, or policy. Any connection is too indirect to register.
No content related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues appears in the bill.
The resolution contains no provisions or references concerning immigration, border policy, or immigrant protections.
No language or implications regarding reproductive rights or abortion access are present.
The bill does not address military, defense, or national security spending or policy.
Although infrastructure and roadway design are mentioned, the resolution does not engage with environmental regulations, climate policy, or environmental protections.
No references to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies exist in the text.
The resolution does not discuss schools, education funding, or education policy.
The preamble cites alcohol-impaired driving statistics, but the operative clauses contain no drug policy, enforcement, or decriminalization measures.
Mentions of speeding and impaired driving are statistical only; the resolution proposes no changes to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice procedures.
No content related to trade, tariffs, or globalization is included.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions or references concerning LGBTQ+ rights or protections appear.
The resolution contains nothing related to foreign aid or international assistance.
No election, voting access, or electoral integrity measures are mentioned.
Advanced vehicle technologies are referenced in the preamble, but the bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight of tech companies.
The text does not engage with labor rights, unions, or workplace policy.
No content relating to religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy is present.
